name: Philip Stroisch
headline: Chief of Staff at CureVac
summary:
My mission is to translate science and technology into products and patient benefit. Guided by hands-on experience in both private and public companies across the Atlantic, I help build organizations that aim to improve lives.

I have led and contributed to initiatives spanning strategy and portfolio management, a successful Nasdaq IPO, business and operating model (re)design, as well as strategic restructuring and cost transformation resulting in multi-year cash runway extension.

Trained as an industrial engineer with additional degrees in management and technology, I have also completed core studies in biomedical science - driven by a passion for lifelong learning and a pursuit to bridge science, technology and business.

positions.title: Head of Investor Relations and Corporate Communications
positions.description: Leading investor relations and corporate communications team ad interim to drive equity story, manage newsflow and ensure aligned messaging across internal and external platforms and channels.

positions.title: Program Head Strategic Restructuring and Transformation
positions.description: Led strategic restructuring including workforce reduction of approximately 30% following new licensing agreement with GSK, re-focusing on research, development, and innovation to create leaner and more agile organization with focus on high-value mRNA pipeline opportunities.

positions.title: Chief of Staff
positions.description: Partnering with CureVac’s CEO and leadership team to advance a new class of mRNA-based medicines in oncology and infectious diseases. Leading the CEO Office with a focus on corporate planning and enabling effective decision-making through lean governance. Sucessfully facilitated CEO transition and onboarding of new company leadership.

positions.title: Head of Portfolio and Project Management Office
positions.description: Led and coached team of ten direct reports to establish enterprise-wide portfolio strategy and execution capability, redefining processes and advancing SAP EPPM to enable data-driven decision-making across the portfolio.

positions.title: Program Head RNA Printer
positions.description: Led company creation project to establish integrated and automated manufacturing solution for mRNA vaccines and therapeutics based on The RNA Printer® engineered in collaboration with Tesla Automation.

positions.title: Entrepreneur in Residence
positions.description: Co-led company creation project for novel cell therapy platform to modulate immune responses in key inflammatory diseases.

positions.title: Director of Corporate Development and Strategy
positions.description: Helped advance U.S.-headquartered regenerative medicine and cell therapy company from preclinical to pivotal stage. Prepared transition from R&D-focused venture to commercially integrated organization as a member of the senior leadership team reporting to the CEO, former CFO of Fresenius Medical Care North America. Led pipeline strategy, market access and organizational development projects contributing to $43m financing for clinical program following the FDA’s regulatory pathway. Headed business development activities resulting in collaborations with key industry and academic partners. Steered public relations team and supported CFO in investor relation activities. Managed and reorganized joint venture in animal health market. Shaped people operations as a member of the recruiting and performance management committee.

company.name: CureVac
company.tagline: We fight for human health - we are the RNA people
company.description: CureVac (Nasdaq: CVAC) is a pioneering multinational biotech company founded in 2000 to advance the field of messenger RNA (mRNA) technology for application in human medicine. In more than two decades of developing, optimizing, and manufacturing this versatile biological molecule for medical purposes, CureVac has introduced and refined key underlying technologies that were essential to the production of mRNA vaccines against COVID-19, and is currently laying the groundwork for application of mRNA in new therapeutic areas of major unmet need. CureVac is leveraging mRNA technology, combined with advanced omics and computational tools, to design and develop off-the-shelf and personalized cancer vaccine product candidates. It also develops programs in prophylactic vaccines and in treatments that enable the human body to produce its own therapeutic proteins. Headquartered in Tübingen, Germany, CureVac also operates sites in the Netherlands, Belgium, Switzerland, and the U.S. Further information can be found at www.curevac.com.
